title: Real-space construction and selection rules of center-of-mass momentum eigenstates in two-dimensional many-body lattices
authors: Ling Lin, Yongguan Ke, Chaohong Lee
abstract: We present a comprehensive framework for the real-space construction of center-of-mass (c.m.) momentum eigenstates in two-dimensional (2D) quantum many-body systems. Unlike standard momentum-space approaches, our real-space formalism explicitly captures the non-uniformity of cyclic subspace dimensions, which are fundamentally governed by the spatial symmetries of the many-body configurations and particle statistics. We demonstrate that performing 2D real-space translations on multi-particle states naturally induces non-trivial translation phase factors associated with the characters of these stabilizer subgroups, leading to a renormalization of permissible momentum values. Notably, we identify an anomalous cross-dimensional momentum coupling in highly symmetric particle distributions, where the permissible momentum values in one direction are strictly constrained by those in the perpendicular direction. We emphasize the algorithmic necessity of this coupling, as neglecting it leads to missing or duplicated basis states in numerical implementations. Concrete examples are provided to demonstrate the practical implementation and physical consequences of this framework.
summary: This paper introduces a novel real-space method for constructing momentum eigenstates in 2D quantum many-body lattices, overcoming limitations of traditional momentum-space techniques. It rigorously derives momentum selection rules based on lattice symmetries and particle statistics. The key finding is the necessity of accounting for anomalous cross-dimensional momentum coupling, which is crucial for accurate numerical simulations of correlated systems.
main_problem: Developing a rigorous framework to construct center-of-mass momentum eigenstates for quantum many-body systems in two dimensions.
main_result: The authors establish that the real-space construction reveals anomalous cross-dimensional momentum coupling, imposing strict selection rules on permissible momentum values.
method: The work develops a real-space formalism that constructs momentum eigenstates by analyzing the cyclic subspaces generated by translation operators acting on a seed state.
model_or_system: The study focuses on two-dimensional quantum many-body lattices, using models like the Bose-Hubbard model, and comparing real-space versus momentum-space descriptions.
key_observables: Center-of-mass (c.m.) momentum ($\mathbf{K}$), cyclic subspace dimensions, and translation phase factors ($\Theta$).
important_parameters: Lattice dimensions ($L_x, L_y$), particle number ($N$), and interaction/hopping parameters (e.g., $U/t$ for Bose-Hubbard).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the real-space approach correctly captures the underlying symmetries and constraints missed by standard momentum-space methods.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares eigenvalues for the Bose-Hubbard model using both methods; Figure 2 compares the sparsity of non-zero matrix elements as a function of particle number, favoring the real-space method.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the momentum-space method, details the novel real-space construction framework, presents numerical comparisons using the Bose-Hubbard model, and concludes by discussing the physical implications of the derived selection rules.
why_interesting: The focus on lattice symmetries, momentum quantization, and the comparison of basis representations is highly relevant to understanding topological phases and ground states in ultracold atoms or solid-state systems.
